label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2, when the agent picks a1 (model-based switch toward S1)
explanation: Fires only at GO (100% of mass). It needs the previous trial to be unrewarded (prev_reward==0 carries 99.7% of mass) and to have ended in S2. In that case the model-based move is to choose a1, whose common state is S1, and the feature fires when the agent policy picks a1 (model_act==1; mass is concentrated at choice logit > 8). The predicate is perfectly precise when prev_state==2 is known. prev_state != 1 also lets in the window first trial, whose previous state is unknown. It does NOT fire at D1/D2, after rewarded trials, or after unrewarded visits to S1 even when a1 is chosen; those were the false positives of the simpler prev_reward==0 & a1 predicate. Misses are low-magnitude activations (bottom quartile) at GO after S2-unrewarded where the agent still picks a2. All variables are observed at GO: model_act is the agent own upcoming choice.

issues: The label's gloss 'model-based switch toward S1' is wrong for most of the feature's activity. Split by previous action (dev): prev a1 -> rare -> S2, unrewarded gives P 1.000, R 0.505, mass 0.680, and covers 0.79 / 0.81 of the top two activation quartiles. That case calls for a model-based STAY on a1. The real switch case, prev a2 -> common -> S2, unrewarded, then a1, gives P 1.000, R 0.121, mass 0.103, and covers only 0.40 / 0.03 / 0.00 of quartiles 2-4, so its activations are weak. In the profile, stay==1 holds 72% of the mass and stay==0 only 10%. The strong firing is 'a1 again after an unrewarded rare transition', not a switch.

The extensional claims check out. Activation is 100% at GO. prev_reward==0 holds 99.7% of the mass. Unrewarded visits to S1 with a1 chosen: P 0.037, mass 0.000. prev_state==2 & a1 has dev precision 1.000. Allowing prev_state==-1 raises dev F1 from 0.768 to 0.841. Test scores reproduce (P 0.934, R 0.737, F1 0.824, mass 0.947).

Systematic misses (5.3% of mass on test): weak activations at GO after an unrewarded visit to S2 where the agent picks a2 but its choice logit is only moderately negative. The threshold model_act==1 (choice > 0) is too strict. Lowering it to choice > -6 recovers most of them: dev F1 0.912, test P 0.905, R 0.920, F1 0.912, mass 0.997.

Systematic false positives sit almost entirely at the window's first trial (rel -3, prev_state unknown), where the previous trial may have ended in S1. They are an artifact of the window, not a property of the feature.

The explanation says 'the model-based response to that history is to choose a1', which treats both S2 paths as switches. It misses that the dominant path (a1 rare) is a repeat. All predicate variables are observable at GO (choice is the agent's own policy logit), so the future-variable claim holds.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step after an unrewarded visit to S2 when the policy leans toward a1. It fires strongest when a1 led to S2 by a rare transition and the agent repeats a1 (a model-based stay); it fires weakly after a2 -> common S2 unrewarded -> switch to a1.
